The larger the angle θ between the two slings the greater each anchor's share: at θ=0 the two anchors take 0.5F each, at 60° about 0.58F, at 90° about 0.71F, and at 120° it reaches 1.0F, while beyond 120° it grows sharply far beyond the total load. Keep the angle within 60° and never exceed 120° at any time.

Increasing spacing therefore reduces the number of placements but makes each bolt carry more load; real placements must be decided together with the bolt rated strength, rock quality and fall factor.
